title: Cluster 02 Drill — Gene Expression and Its Control
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 2 · 9 questions · 118 marks · cumulative over Cluster 1 + Cluster 2 + Book 1
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b) - that is the point of the layout.

Every stem is one or two sentences and every answer is long. No stem lists the axes to compare on, no stem tells you which option is wrong, and no stem contains the answer. Every question is built on a real prelim, specimen or topical-bank question, and every figure is the real image from the document it came from, not a redrawing.

Cumulative. Five parts need Cluster 1 said cold - Q1(a) the replication enzymes and why a lagging strand exists, Q2 base pairing and strand polarity, Q3(b) introns as non-coding DNA, Q5(a) the whole packing hierarchy, Q6(b) enhancers and silencers inside an intron. Three parts reach into Book 1 - Q1(b) the enzyme active site, Q4 primary structure deciding tertiary structure, Q8(b) the four levels of protein structure and which bonds survive denaturation. A Cluster 1 or Book 1 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Cluster 2 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Ordered steps earn ordered marks: an enzyme without its exact job, or the job without the enzyme, scores nothing. Direction is a mark every time - 5' to 3' synthesis, template read 3' to 5', ribosome moving 5' to 3', polypeptide built N-terminus to C-terminus. Say polypeptide, never protein, as the product of translation. Activators and repressors are proteins; enhancers and silencers are DNA.
los_html:
Learning outcomes this cluster owns (9477 Core Idea 2)
2(a) structure and roles of DNA and RNA (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA)Q2, Q4
2(c) transcription, pre-mRNA to mRNA, translationQ1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q8
2(i) i chromatin level: histone modification, DNA methylationQ5, Q9
2(i) ii transcriptional level: control elements and transcription factorsQ6, Q9
2(i) iii post-transcriptional level: splicing, polyadenylation, 5' cappingQ3, Q9
2(i) iv translational level: half-life of RNA, initiation of translationQ7, Q9
2(i) v post-translational level: biochemical modification, protein degradationQ8, Q9
reach-back 2(b) replication and its enzymes (Cluster 1)Q1
reach-back 2(d) and 2(h) DNA packing and non-coding DNA (Cluster 1)Q5, Q6, Q3
reach-back Core Idea 1 protein structure and enzymes (Book 1)Q1, Q4, Q8

Two traps here carry measured failure rates from real examiner reports: the alternative-splicing rules in Q3(a), answered correctly by only 33.12% of the cohort, and the mitochondrial code count in Q2(a), where candidates count codons rather than peptide bonds. LO 2(i) is the largest outcome in Book 2 - 234 questions in the bank, 95 at the hardest tier - and it names five levels. A pass that covers three has covered 60% of it, so Q9 is the one to sit last and sit properly.

RNA interference is cut. No learning outcome in Core Idea 2 mentions miRNA, siRNA, Dicer or RISC, so no question here needs it and it is never a valid answer at the translational level.
